description: verification-architecture.md's '## Gate' section (the section explicitly titled as what 'Phase 3 (adversarial review) must confirm' before this increment can be considered adversarially cleared) is an enumerated, closed-looking checklist -- items (1), (2), (3), (4), (4a), (4b), (5) -- covering REQ-101, REQ-102, REQ-103, REQ-201, REQ-203, and REQ-301. It contains NO corresponding item for REQ-202 (automatic, non-sticky catalog restoration once above the reserve) or REQ-302 (the research spike must not gate the parallel gig-board witness track), even though both requirements have their own dedicated proof obligations earlier in the same document (PROP-202a at line 90, PROP-202b at line 91, both 'required: true'; PROP-302a at line 96, 'required: true') and both are separately named in the Verification Strategy tier breakdown (REQ-301/302's non-blocking check is bundled into the Tier-0 bullet at lines 103-105; REQ-202's two-wake wiring test is named in the Tier-2 bullet at lines 119-121). The Gate section's own framing -- an imperative, numbered '(1)...(5)' list introduced by 'must confirm' -- invites a Phase 3 reviewer to treat it as the exhaustive, closed set of confirmation steps required to clear this increment, exactly the same 'closed enumerated list that turns out to omit a real item' failure mode that already produced three consecutive Phase-1c FAILs in this exact feature's own history (FIND-201's four-phrase list missing a fifth phrase; FIND-301's 'block + what it references' scope missing the sibling MINDSET section; FIND-401's 'closed four-part list' missing buildUserMessage entirely) -- except this time the omitted items are not phrases inside prompt.mjs but two entire REQUIREMENTS (REQ-202, REQ-302) missing from the increment's own final sign-off checklist. A Phase 3 adversary who follows the Gate section literally (as its own imperative wording invites) could complete items (1)-(5) with a real, defensible sense of 'the Gate is satisfied' while never being explicitly directed to confirm REQ-202's balance-oscillation/non-sticky-restoration behavior or REQ-302's non-blocking-dependency guarantee -- even though both PROPs are marked 'required: true' in the Proof Obligations table two sections earlier in the same file. This is an internal inconsistency between two parts of the SAME verification-architecture.md document (the Proof Obligations table + Verification Strategy section, which both cover all 8 REQs, versus the Gate section, which covers only 6 of the 8), not a hypothetical -- it exists in the current text as written, independent of and unrelated to the REQ-204 scope cut.

evidence.snippet:
## Gate

Phase 3 (adversarial review) must confirm, via fresh-context, disk-only review plus (for PROP-102 and PROP-103) live/testnet re-execution performed by the adversary itself:
(1) REQ-101's heartbeat/atomicity properties... (2) REQ-102's shared-file protection... (3) REQ-103's full existing test suite... (4) REQ-201/203's catalog filter is read end-to-end... (4a) `skills/registry.json` has an explicit `risk`/`alwaysAvailable` value... (4b) `hasOpenRiskPositionOf` is actually implemented... (5) REQ-301's research record is spot-checked against the actual current state...
[document ends at line 183 -- no (6) item, no explicit REQ-202 or REQ-302 confirmation step anywhere in this section]

crossReference.snippet: PROP-202a (line 90, tier 1, required: true) | PROP-202b (line 91, tier 1/2, required: true) -- REQ-202's own proof obligations, never referenced by name anywhere in the Gate section. PROP-302a (line 96, tier 0, required: true) -- REQ-302's own proof obligation, likewise absent from the Gate section's numbered list. Verification Strategy Tier 0 bullet (lines 103-105) names 'REQ-301/302's research-record existence/citation/non-blocking checks' and Tier 2 bullet (lines 119-121) names 'REQ-202's two-wake balance-transition wiring test through index.mjs' -- proving both requirements were clearly intended to be verified, just never carried through into the Gate section's own closed enumeration.
